budget_items.topic: 925 Mass Ave gas station RFP / brownfields cleanup
budget_items.what_was_said: The director reported MRPC brownfield funding paid for a consultant to develop a recommended cleanup option, a cost estimate, a timeframe, and a list of funding sources ahead of the town's RFP for the property.
The board wants a cash bond rather than a surety bond to cover remaining loam and seeding work, with a contingency escalator built into the bond up front.
The applicant's engineer said there may be no money left in the 53G account funding peer review, and the account will likely need to be replenished for further lots.

budget_items.topic: 860 New West Townsend Road 53G peer-review account
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant proactively set up a 53G account to fund a peer-review consultant given the timing of the conservation commission filing.

budget_items.topic: Town budget deficit and commercial development
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member argued the town can't afford to reject chain businesses given the town's budget deficit and limited commercial land.
The town planner called the current fee schedule overly complicated and said he would bring a simplified version to the board.

budget_items.topic: Housing production plan / one-stop growth grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The town planner is updating the expired housing production plan, which extends safe-harbor status by creating units, while MRPC applies for a one-stop growth grant after an earlier DTA application went unfunded.

budget_items.topic: District Local Technical Assistance grant - buildout analysis
budget_items.what_was_said: A DLTA grant from MRPC will fund a review of remaining developable commercial and industrial land against the town's older buildout maps, expected by end of summer.

budget_items.topic: Master plan consultant contract - final presentation
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed whether to require a formal final presentation from the master plan consultant, noting one is already included in the existing contract.

The Capital Planning Committee could not meet to finalize capital numbers because the town budget wasn't ready, amid what was described as a severe budget challenge and a past shortage of budgeting staff.
Montachusett Regional Planning Commission business included approving member travel and allocating money to hire another planner.

decisions.decision: 10 Parmentor Road applicant's counsel agreed to discuss with the client whether to split the 25-lot storm water/driveway permits into fewer, phased applications rather than filing them lot-by-lot.

For 10 Parmentor Road, the board indicated it would accept a plan note stating Lot 1 is to be conveyed to the abutting Perkins Revocable Trust property (rather than standing as a separate buildable lot) to resolve the frontage/cul-de-sac issue.
For 860 New West Townsend Road, the applicant agreed to set up a meeting with the fire chief to review the common driveway/fire-truck turnaround concerns before the continued hearing.
Staff will obtain a copy of the ZBA decision approving the townhome use at 860 New West Townsend Road and add it to the project file.
The board will forward Adam's and Amanda's written comments on the draft master plan to the consultant (Over&Under) to finish the document, rather than have every comment individually re-debated.
The board decided it does not need a formal ceremonial presentation from the master plan consultant once the plan is finalized.

The board settled on four zoning amendments to pursue before the next annual town meeting: rewriting inclusionary zoning, a senior housing bylaw, minor site plan review, and a cluster-development-by-right bylaw.
The scenic road bylaw and a town signage bylaw were pushed off to a second year of zoning work rather than pursued this year.

minutes.headline: Planning Board sets its FY27 zoning-amendment priorities and continues two housing hearings pending fire/engineering review
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board acted on several site-plan and ANR matters, including continuing a 20-unit townhome project on New West Townsend Road pending fire department and peer-engineering review, approving de minimis changes for a solar array and a garage rebuild, and declining the town's first right of refusal on Chapter land. The bulk of the meeting was spent giving detailed feedback on the draft master plan and agreeing on the town planner's 2026 work program, settling on four zoning amendments (inclusionary zoning, senior housing, minor site plan review, and a cluster-development bylaw) to pursue before the next annual town meeting.

what_happened.line: The board settled on four zoning amendments to bring to the next annual town meeting: inclusionary zoning, senior housing, minor site plan review, and cluster development.
The 20-unit townhome project on New West Townsend Road was continued to mid-April pending fire department review of the driveway and engineering review.
The board advised the select board to decline the town's first right of refusal on Chapter land at Northfield Road.
De minimis site plan changes were approved for a rooftop solar/battery project and for a garage rebuild.

why_it_matters: The zoning amendments, if brought to town meeting, would change rules for housing density, senior housing, and small-project review townwide.
The continued hearing means the townhome project's fire-access and engineering questions are unresolved and will return for another public hearing.
Declining the right of first refusal clears the way for the Northfield Road land to be sold or developed privately rather than held or acquired by the town.
watch_next: Continued hearings for the townhome project and other applications, 13 April 2026
Zoning amendments proposed for the next annual town meeting
